minutes.headline: Sewer Commission adopted the amended irrigation meter policy; the engineering bid went to counsel before any vote.
minutes.summary: The commission elected officers, reviewed the maintenance plan kickoff, and scored the only bid for an inflow and infiltration study. Members debated the study's cost and asked counsel whether the contract can be negotiated. They worked through irrigation meter implementation and then approved the amended policy after a resident objected that no new hearing was held. They also covered the operator contract review, audit agents, solar credits, and a closed session on litigation.

what_happened.line: The commission approved the irrigation meter policy as amended with the evening's changes, after a resident objected that no new public hearing was held.
Members scored the only bid for a third-party inflow and infiltration study and agreed the business manager will ask town counsel whether the contract can be negotiated.
Commissioners will ask counsel whether they can do on-site grease trap audits, with an answer wanted by June 11th.
The commission elected officers, with a nomination for chair heard at the start of the meeting.
The operator contract review was deferred to June 11th, and the commission later entered executive session on litigation.

why_it_matters: The amended irrigation meter policy sets how outdoor water use is metered and billed on sewer accounts, so it can change what some households pay.
The study bid and operator contract are costs the commission can pass to ratepayers through sewer rates, and both remain undecided until a vote on June 11th.
watch_next: June 11th meeting: the vote on the study contract, the operator contract review, and counsel's answer on on-site audits.
